short: A square that none of your pawns can ever attack again.
body: Every pawn move is permanent, and every pawn move gives up the squares that pawn used to guard. When a square in your own half can no longer be attacked by any pawn, it is a hole, and an enemy piece that reaches it cannot be driven away.
Holes are created, not found. Provoking a pawn move is a real plan: attack something so that it must be defended by a pawn advance, and the square behind that pawn becomes yours.
A hole on your side of the board that one of your pawns protects is an [[outpost]] — the same square seen from the other direction.

diagram.caption: Black's pawns on e5 and a6 will leave d5 and b5 permanently unguardable.
